From 059b7dbd20a6f0c539a45ddff1573cb8946685b5 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Eric Dumazet <edumazet@google.com>
Date: Thu, 30 Apr 2026 12:26:52 +0000
Subject: [PATCH] vsock/virtio: fix potential unbounded skb queue
MIME-Version: 1.0
Content-Type: text/plain; charset=UTF-8
Content-Transfer-Encoding: 8bit

virtio_transport_inc_rx_pkt() checks vvs->rx_bytes + len > vvs->buf_alloc.

virtio_transport_recv_enqueue() skips coalescing for packets
with VIRTIO_VSOCK_SEQ_EOM.

If fed with packets with len == 0 and VIRTIO_VSOCK_SEQ_EOM,
a very large number of packets can be queued
because vvs->rx_bytes stays at 0.

Fix this by estimating the skb metadata size:

	(Number of skbs in the queue) * SKB_TRUESIZE(0)

Fixes: 077706165717 ("virtio/vsock: don't use skbuff state to account credit")
Signed-off-by: Eric Dumazet <edumazet@google.com>
Cc: Arseniy Krasnov <AVKrasnov@sberdevices.ru>
Cc: Stefan Hajnoczi <stefanha@redhat.com>
Cc: Stefano Garzarella <sgarzare@redhat.com>
Cc: "Michael S. Tsirkin" <mst@redhat.com>
Cc: Jason Wang <jasowang@redhat.com>
Cc: Xuan Zhuo <xuanzhuo@linux.alibaba.com>
Cc: "Eugenio Pérez" <eperezma@redhat.com>
Cc: virtualization@lists.linux.dev
Link: https://patch.msgid.link/20260430122653.554058-1-edumazet@google.com
Signed-off-by: Jakub Kicinski <kuba@kernel.org>

diff --git a/net/vmw_vsock/virtio_transport_common.c b/net/vmw_vsock/virtio_transport_common.c
index 416d533f493d..9b8014516f4f 100644
--- a/net/vmw_vsock/virtio_transport_common.c
+++ b/net/vmw_vsock/virtio_transport_common.c
@@ -447,7 +447,9 @@ static int virtio_transport_send_pkt_info(struct vsock_sock *vsk,
 static bool virtio_transport_inc_rx_pkt(struct virtio_vsock_sock *vvs,
 					u32 len)
 {
-	if (vvs->buf_used + len > vvs->buf_alloc)
+	u64 skb_overhead = (skb_queue_len(&vvs->rx_queue) + 1) * SKB_TRUESIZE(0);
+
+	if (skb_overhead + vvs->buf_used + len > vvs->buf_alloc)
 		return false;
 
 	vvs->rx_bytes += len;
-- 
2.34.1

The patch fixes a vulnerability in the virtio-vsock transport where an unbounded number of small skbs (specifically zero-length packets with `VIRTIO_VSOCK_SEQ_EOM`) could be queued, causing resource exhaustion. The change ensures that the memory overhead of the skb structures themselves is factored into the credit accounting.

**File modified:** `net/vmw_vsock/virtio_transport_common.c`

**Modification in the function `virtio_transport_inc_rx_pkt`:**
- Before the fix, only `buf_used + len` was compared against `buf_alloc`.
- After the fix, an overhead term `(skb_queue_len(&vvs->rx_queue) + 1) * SKB_TRUESIZE(0)` is added to account for the approximate kernel memory used by the skb metadata for all queued skbs (including the one being added). The check now becomes `skb_overhead + buf_used + len > buf_alloc`.

**Relationship:**
The bug occurred because `virtio_transport_recv_enqueue` skips coalescing for packets with `VIRTIO_VSOCK_SEQ_EOM`. If such packets have `len == 0`, then `buf_used` (which tracks payload bytes) never increases, so the credit check always passes, allowing an unlimited number of these small skbs to accumulate. The fix indirectly caps the queue length by reserving credit for each skb's memory footprint (the `SKB_TRUESIZE(0)` overhead). This prevents the unbounded growth without changing the actual payload accounting.

Here is the root cause:
The credit check in `virtio_transport_inc_rx_pkt` only compared the sum of payload bytes (`buf_used + len`) against `buf_alloc`. Zero-length packets with `VIRTIO_VSOCK_SEQ_EOM` bypassed coalescing and added skbs without increasing `buf_used`. Since the overhead of skb metadata was not accounted for, the check always passed, allowing an unbounded number of such skbs to be queued, leading to resource exhaustion.

Here is the patch:
 
 static bool virtio_transport_inc_rx_pkt(struct virtio_vsock_sock *vvs,
 					u32 len)
 {
-	if (vvs->buf_used + len > vvs->buf_alloc)
+	u64 skb_overhead = (skb_queue_len(&vvs->rx_queue) + 1) * SKB_TRUESIZE(0);
+
+	if (skb_overhead + vvs->buf_used + len > vvs->buf_alloc)
 		return false;
 
 	vvs->rx_bytes += len;
 	vvs->buf_used += len;
 	return true;
 }

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
<text>if (vvs->buf_used + len > vvs->buf_alloc)</text>
Reason:
This check only compares payload bytes against the credit limit. For packets with `len == 0` and `VIRTIO_VSOCK_SEQ_EOM`, `buf_used` never increases, so the condition always passes, allowing an unbounded number of such packets to be queued without accounting for the memory used by the skb structures themselves.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
<text>u64 skb_overhead = (skb_queue_len(&vvs->rx_queue) + 1) * SKB_TRUESIZE(0);</text>
<text>if (skb_overhead + vvs->buf_used + len > vvs->buf_alloc)</text>
Reason:
The fix adds the estimated skb metadata overhead to the credit check. `SKB_TRUESIZE(0)` represents the memory consumed by an empty skb. Multiplying by (current queue length + 1) accounts for the skbs already queued and the incoming one. This ensures that even zero-length packets consume credit for their skb overhead, preventing unbounded queue growth.
